title: Existence of an ample invertible module descends along field extensions
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $K/k$ a field extension [def-pc-field-extension], and $X$ a $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Put $X_K=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. If there exists an invertible $\mathcal O_{X_K}$-module which is ample in the absolute sense [def-sc-invertible-module, def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], then there exists an absolutely ample invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module. No finite-type, separatedness, algebraicity or finiteness assumption on $K/k$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0BDC, lemma-ample-after-field-extension (existence, not descent of a specified invertible module).

proof.text: Choose an ample invertible module $L$ on $X_K$. By [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], $X_K$ is quasi-compact. The map $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is surjective by [lem-pc-field-extension-surjective]; its base changes $X_K\to X$ and $W_K\to W$ for every open subscheme $W\subseteq X$ are surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. The continuous-image result [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-image-quasi-compact] applied to $X_K\to X$ makes $X$ quasi-compact.

The ample-module criterion [lem-weil-pbc-ample-scheme-separated] and [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated] make $X_K$ quasi-separated. If $U,V\subseteq X$ are affine opens, their scalar extensions are affine: [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies them with the spectra of $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O)\otimes_kK$ and $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O)\otimes_kK$. Thus $U_K\cap V_K=(U\cap V)_K$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-separated-affine-cover-criterion](1). Its surjection onto $U\cap V$ from step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-image-quasi-compact] show that $U\cap V$ is quasi-compact. Apply clause (2) of the same affine-cover criterion to the cover of $X$ by all its affine opens: $X$ is quasi-separated.

Let $I$ be the set of finitely generated $k$-subalgebras $A_i\subseteq K$, ordered by inclusion. It is small and nonempty (it contains $k$), any two members lie in the subalgebra generated by the union of their finite generating sets, and every element of $K$ lies in $k[a]$. Thus the union, hence the ring colimit, is $K$. By [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition] the affine system $\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ has limit $\operatorname{Spec}K$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-over-limit] with initial stage $\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $T=X$: the schemes $X_i=X\times_k\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ have affine transitions and limit $X_K$. Each projection $X_i\to X$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](1) applied to $\operatorname{Spec}A_i\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. It is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by clause (3), so [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](2) and steps 1--2 show that every $X_i$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

Apply [lem-trf-invertible-affine-limit-descent] to this small directed system of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes with affine transitions. It supplies an index $i$ and an invertible module $L_i$ on $X_i$ whose pullback is $L$. Apply [lem-trf-ample-affine-limit-descent] on the tail $j\geq i$: after replacing $i$ by some later $j$ and $L_i$ by its pullback, $L_i$ is ample. This uses the same absolute ampleness notion as the hypothesis, without assuming that $X$ is of finite type over $k$.

The algebra $A_i$ is nonzero because it is a subalgebra of the field $K$. Choose a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\subset A_i$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal] applied to the zero ideal. Put $k^{\prime}=A_i/\mathfrak m$. It is a field and a finitely generated $k$-algebra, since the images of any finite generating set of $A_i$ generate its quotient. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-lemma] makes $k^{\prime}/k$ a finite field extension.

The quotient map $A_i\twoheadrightarrow k^{\prime}$ defines a closed immersion $\operatorname{Spec}k^{\prime}\to\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ by the affine characterization in [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Its base change $j:X_{k^{\prime}}\to X_i$ is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Therefore $M=j^*L_i$ is ample by [lem-trf-ample-restrict-closed-immersion].

Write $d=[k^{\prime}:k]\geq1$ and choose a $k$-basis $e_1,\ldots,e_d$ of $k^{\prime}$. On each affine open $\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq X$, [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies the inverse image under $f:X_{k^{\prime}}\to X$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_kk^{\prime})$. The elements $1\otimes e_r$ form a $B$-basis, so this algebra is finite and flat, the latter by [lem-sc-affine-standard-cover-finite-free-local-fp-flat]. For finite presentation, write $e_re_s=\sum_tc_{rst}e_t$ and $1=\sum_tu_te_t$. The algebra has the finite presentation $B[T_1,\ldots,T_d]/(T_rT_s-\sum_tc_{rst}T_t,\ 1-\sum_tu_tT_t)$: the relations reduce every polynomial to a linear combination of the $T_t$, and independence of the $1\otimes e_t$ makes the resulting surjection injective. Thus $f$ is finite, flat and locally of finite presentation, hence finite locally free by [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. It is surjective by [lem-pc-field-extension-surjective] and [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change].

Apply [lem-sfb-finite-locally-free-ample-existence] to the surjective finite locally free map $f:X_{k^{\prime}}\to X$ of step 7 and the ample invertible module $M$ of step 6. Its conclusion supplies an absolutely ample invertible module on $X$. The selected module need not pull back to the original $L$; only existence is asserted, exactly as required.
